name:Clear dome (cornea): A thin transparent corneal dome has a curved front and fine tissue edge, seen obliquely so its cap shape is visible.
name:Light-sensitive cells: A broad cup-shaped layer of photoreceptor tissue has a curved inner surface and closely aligned fine rods and cones along its cut edge.
name:Retinal nerve cells: A broad cup-shaped layer of retinal neural tissue carries branching fibres that gather into an attached outgoing optic nerve.
name:Retina with optic nerve: The photoreceptor and neural tissue layers form one broad curved retinal lining within supplied supporting eye wall, with fibres gathering into its attached optic nerve. No duplicate magnified strip is shown.
name:Outer ears and canals: One representative outer ear and canal appear in cutaway, with their actual cartilage, skin and surrounding tissue continuing around the open middle-ear cavity. No vibration arrows or head silhouette accompany them.
name:Coiled inner-ear chambers and fluid: A cochlear chamber is opened along its coil, exposing fluid and its tissue partition continuously within the spiral. A small bounded oval window is visible at its base. The partition has room for its sensory tissue; no detached enlargement or missing-part symbol appears.
name:Turning sensor cells: Three prepared sensory ridges carry hair-bearing cells beneath broad translucent jelly partitions. Their differing shapes match the full cross-sections of the three widened duct chambers.
name:Tilt sensor cells: Two separate sensory tissue patches carry hair cells whose bundles project into soft translucent jelly layers. One patch lies horizontally and the other stands vertically; neither contains mineral crystals yet.
name:Fluid-filled loops: Three narrow fluid-filled ducts occupy different, roughly perpendicular planes. An oblique cutaway shows a foreshortened horizontal loop crossing in front of two differently oriented vertical loops, each with an exposed widened chamber.
name:Turn-sensing canals: The sensory ridges and broad jelly partitions occupy the widened duct chambers. Each partition spans its chamber and meets the surrounding tissue wall; the three loops retain their distinct spatial planes.
